blocks.text: Built an end-to-end AI pipeline that turns thousands of unstructured Amazon reviews into structured product insights — common complaints, top praise, feature requests, sentiment breakdowns, and evidence-backed recommendations. Processed 20,000+ reviews with 99% valid structured outputs and 98% source-backed accuracy. Compressed analysis from hours to minutes using a Large Language Model (LLM) — an AI system trained to understand and generate text.
Problem

Product teams often have thousands of reviews but no practical way to turn them into decisions. Manual tagging takes hours. Generic sentiment tools only tell you whether customers are positive or negative — not what they're complaining about, what they love, or what to build next.
Manual review tagging created inconsistent categories across reviewers and took hours per product.
Off-the-shelf sentiment tools produced polarity scores (positive/negative) but no product-specific insight.
Thousands of reviews cannot fit into a single model prompt due to model input limits, so a batching and combining strategy was required.
Teams needed structured outputs they could act on — not summaries, but data usable in dashboards, exports, or planning docs.
Users & Stakeholders

items.title: Product Managers
items.description: Prioritizing roadmap opportunities based on what customers actually complain about or ask for.

items.title: Founders
items.description: Validating product-market fit signals across large sets of real customer feedback.

items.title: CX Teams
items.description: Identifying recurring complaint categories to reduce support volume and improve response quality.

items.title: Growth Teams
items.description: Finding positioning and messaging opportunities from what customers praise most.

items.title: Marketplace Sellers
items.description: Improving listings and products based on structured review intelligence.

blocks.text: Product Goal
Compress hours of manual review analysis into minutes while keeping every insight traceable to real customer reviews — so teams can trust the output and act on it.
How It Works

An LLM pipeline that cleans, processes, and extracts structured insights from large sets of reviews in batches. The LLM is prompted to return fixed structured outputs using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), a standard data format — rather than free-form summaries. This makes the output directly usable in dashboards, exports, and planning docs without extra processing. Every insight is tied back to evidence from real reviews.

items.title: Import & Clean
items.description: Reviews are imported, normalized, and deduplicated. Low-quality or spam entries are filtered before processing.

items.title: Split Into Batches
items.description: Thousands of reviews are divided into smaller groups that fit within model input limits, so the LLM can process the full dataset consistently.

items.title: Structured Output Extraction
items.description: The LLM is prompted with a fixed JSON structure to extract themes, sentiment, complaints, praise, and feature requests from each batch in a consistent, machine-readable format.

items.title: Automated Validation
items.description: Each batch output is checked for valid JSON structure and source-backed accuracy — catching any outputs that are malformed or contain unsupported claims.

items.title: Combine Results
items.description: Results from all batches are combined to surface themes and patterns that appear consistently across the full set of reviews.

items.title: Insight Report
items.description: A final report is generated with supporting evidence from real reviews for each theme — structured for product decisions, not just reading.

blocks.text: Pipeline Workflow
Structured Output Format

Each batch produced output in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), a standard structured data format. Using a fixed output structure meant results could be used directly in dashboards or planning tools without additional processing.
Evaluation & Quality Controls
I built an evaluation set — a test group of reviews with manually verified expected outputs — to measure quality before trusting the pipeline on real datasets.
Structured output validity: did the LLM return clean JSON that could be parsed and used by other tools? Achieved 99% across evaluation sets.
Source-backed accuracy: did the themes and summaries match real reviews in the dataset? Achieved 98% when sampling outputs against source reviews.
Hallucination checks: did the system avoid unsupported claims — themes or summaries not backed by any review in the batch? Explicit checks were run on each output.
Duplicate theme checks: did different batches surface the same theme under different names? The combining step was tested to prevent redundancy.
Batch consistency: did different batches on similar review sets produce consistent outputs? Outputs were compared across batches to catch quality variance.
Human sample review: manually reviewed a sample of AI-generated themes to confirm they matched what a product manager would actually find useful.
Key Product Decisions

blocks.decision: Structured JSON output vs. free-form summaries
blocks.tradeoff: Free-form text summaries are easier to generate but can't be reused in dashboards, exports, or planning docs without extra work.
blocks.outcome: Fixed JSON output made insights directly usable in product tools — no additional processing needed.

blocks.tradeoff: Polished, readable prose can sound convincing but be harder to verify against the original reviews.
blocks.outcome: Prioritized accuracy over readability — every claim is tied to evidence snippets from real reviews so teams can verify before acting.

blocks.tradeoff: Positive/negative sentiment scores are faster to compute but don't tell a PM what to build or fix.
blocks.outcome: Focused on extracting product areas, feature requests, and complaint categories — outputs designed to support roadmap decisions.

blocks.decision: Batch processing with a combining step
blocks.tradeoff: Sending all reviews in one prompt would exceed model input limits and reduce output consistency.
blocks.outcome: Reviews were split into batches and results were combined in a final step — allowing 20,000+ reviews to be processed reliably.

blocks.text: Results & Impact
Processed 20,000+ Amazon product reviews end-to-end.
Achieved 99% valid structured outputs on evaluation sets.
Achieved 98% source-backed accuracy — themes and summaries traced back to real reviews.
Compressed review analysis from hours to minutes per batch run.
Turned unstructured review data into structured, roadmap-ready product intelligence with evidence for every insight.
What I Would Do Next

Add trend detection over time to surface emerging complaints or rising feature demand.
Add severity and opportunity scoring to help teams prioritize themes by likely impact.
Add integrations with Notion, Airtable, or productboard to push insights directly into planning docs.
Add a feedback loop so reviewers can flag or correct AI-generated themes to improve accuracy over time.
